queue.title: F116 spec loop round 1 — explore and propose: forbid extras on TriggerAgentRequest
queue.detail: EXPLORE THE CODE FIRST, then write the proposal. The defect, reproduced live 2026-08-29: POST /projects/{id}/agent/trigger accepts an unknown top-level `permission_mode`, returns 200, silently discards it, and the run proceeds UNSUPERVISED — while the sibling POST /projects/{id}/permission-requests/{id}/decide forbids extras with a 422 that names the right field. Posture actually travels in `overrides`, keyed `permission_mode` (hub/ui/src/api/modelCatalog.ts:56, hub/ui/src/components/agents/AgentOutputPanel.tsx:327-328). Full write-up: FINDINGS.md F116. Smallest honest fix named there: forbid extras on TriggerAgentRequest so the misuse is named rather than absorbed. BEFORE PROPOSING, AUDIT: which other Pydantic request models in hub/hub/schemas/ and hub/hub/api/v1/ allow extras, and is the lax setting a default or a choice? The proposal must say whether the rule belongs on one model or on a shared base — the operator's standing preference is 'always the cleanest solution', and 'more work' is never the objection. Also decide what happens to a client that TODAY sends a harmless unknown field: forbidding extras is a breaking change for them, and the proposal must say so out loud rather than discovering it in round 3.
queue.outcome: Proposed openspec/changes/2026-08-29-an-unknown-field-is-named/ (proposal, design, tasks, delta for a new api-request-strictness capability). validate --strict passes. Audit result: 36 request models forbid extras, 19 do not, and the laxness is the pydantic default everywhere except SpecDocumentCreate, which is lax on purpose and backed by agent-document-creation's 'unexpressible rather than merely refused' requirement — so a blanket sweep would breach a shipped requirement. Chosen shape: a shared RequestModel base plus a test that walks app.routes and carries a named exemption list. D1 resolved: proceed, no shipped client relies on the tolerance.

The route is not publicly documented as tolerant, the only known clients are the Hub's own UI and this repo's harnesses, and the failure it prevents is an unsupervised run the operator believes is supervised.
